request.idea: craete a jbl 4way speaker with one sub with bluetooth module

brief.title: 4-way Bluetooth speaker with subwoofer (JBL-style)
brief.understanding: You want to build a large JBL-style Bluetooth speaker that plays music from a phone and splits the sound across four driver sizes, with one subwoofer for deep bass. I have assumed a single mains-powered cabinet in which the subwoofer is the lowest of the four bands (sub, woofer, midrange, tweeter). This is a home-built speaker in that style, not a copy of a JBL product or its branding.

questions.question: What does "4-way with one sub" mean for you?
options: One box: sub + woofer + mid + tweeter
One box: 4 drivers plus a separate sub
Stereo pair of speakers + one sub box
questions.assumed: One box: sub + woofer + mid + tweeter
questions.why: It sets the number of drivers, amplifier channels and cabinets, and so most of the cost.

questions.question: How should it be powered?
questions.why: A battery adds a 6-cell pack, protection and a charger, and limits how loud it can go.

questions.question: How big and loud should it be?
questions.why: Sub size sets the cabinet volume, amplifier and power supply rating.

questions.question: How should the sound be split between the drivers?
options: Simple: passive crossover parts, no programming
Advanced: DSP board (ADAU1701), tunable on a PC
questions.assumed: Simple: passive crossover parts, no programming
questions.why: DSP sounds better and is tunable, but needs four amplifier channels and software setup.

questions.question: What is your budget for parts, including the wood for the box?
questions.why: Driver quality is the largest cost and the largest factor in how it sounds.

requirements: Bluetooth 5.0 audio from a phone (SBC/AAC), range at least 10 m in open space
Four bands in one cabinet: sub below about 120 Hz, woofer 120-800 Hz, midrange 800 Hz-4 kHz, tweeter above 4 kHz
Amplifier power: about 100 W into the 4 ohm subwoofer, plus 2 x 50 W for the upper drivers
Supply: 24 V DC, 6 A (about 150 W) mains adapter with a barrel jack on the rear panel
Frequency response target: 45 Hz to 20 kHz
Controls: power switch, master volume knob, sub level knob; pairing is handled by the Bluetooth module
Cabinet: 18 mm MDF, about 25-30 litres for the sub chamber, with a sealed separate chamber for the midrange; overall about 30 x 35 x 70 cm
Parts cost for one unit of $150-300 including wood

blocks.name: Power input
blocks.role: Converts wall power to 24 V DC for the amplifier and feeds a small regulator for the Bluetooth module.
blocks.parts: 24 V 6 A desktop adapter (Mean Well GST160A24 class), DC jack, rocker switch, LM2596 buck module to 5 V

blocks.name: Bluetooth receiver
blocks.role: Receives music from the phone and outputs a stereo line-level signal.
blocks.parts: Bluetooth 5.0 audio receiver board with line out (QCC3008 or MH-M28 class)

blocks.name: Mono mix and controls
blocks.role: Sums left and right into one signal with two resistors and sets master volume.
blocks.parts: 2 x 4.7k resistors, 10k log potentiometer, ground-loop isolating 5 V supply (B0505S) if hum appears

blocks.name: 2.1 amplifier
blocks.role: Low-pass filters and amplifies the sub channel (100 W) and amplifies two full-range channels (2 x 50 W).
blocks.parts: TPA3116D2 2.1 amplifier board (XH-M139 class) with a sub level/frequency knob

blocks.name: Passive crossover
blocks.role: Splits the two amplifier channels: one drives the woofer, the other drives the midrange and tweeter, each through its filter.
blocks.parts: Air-core/ferrite inductors and polypropylene film capacitors (12 dB/octave), or a ready-made 3-way crossover board at 80

blocks.name: Drivers
blocks.role: Turn the amplified signal into sound across the four bands.
blocks.parts: 8" 4 ohm 100 W subwoofer, 5.25" 4-8 ohm woofer, 3" midrange, 1" dome tweeter (Dayton Audio, or JBL replacement drivers)

blocks.name: Cabinet
blocks.role: Holds the drivers and provides the tuned air volume the subwoofer needs.
blocks.parts: 18 mm MDF, bass-reflex port tube, damping wadding, speaker terminal wire, rear panel for jack, switch and knobs

risks: Hum or whine when the Bluetooth module shares the amplifier supply: power the module through an isolated 5 V converter and keep signal wires short and shielded.

Crossover does not match the chosen drivers (harsh or missing midrange): pick the drivers first, then calculate the crossover from their real impedance and sensitivity, and add a resistor pad to the tweeter if it is too loud.
Weak or boomy bass from wrong cabinet volume or port length: use the sub's Thiele-Small parameters in a free calculator (WinISD) before cutting wood.
Amplifier overheating or shutting down at high volume: do not go below 4 ohm per channel, leave airflow around the heatsink, and check that the supply can deliver 6 A.
